Response to Comments / Final Environmental Impact Report December 2021
CHAPTER 3
Roster of Commenters
3.0 Introduction
This chapter lists each public agency, organization, and individual that provided comments on the
Draft EIR generally during the public review and comment period for the Draft EIR, which began
on February 26, 2021, and ended at 4:00 p.m. April 27, 2021.1 The comments addressed in Chapter
5 (Responses to Individual Comments) and Chapter 6 (Responses to Public Hearing Comments) of
this Final EIR are presented in the order of the commenters listed below. Commenters have an
alphabetic designation that corresponds to the category of commenter, such as “A” for public
agencies. A number follows the alphabetic designation to indicate the sequence of the comment
submissions. For example, “A-1” is the first public agency comment submission identified, as
shown below.
3.1 Public Agencies
Table 3-1 below lists the State, regional, and local public agencies that submitted comments on
the Draft EIR. As shown in the table, each public agency’s comment submission is identified with
an “A” designation and followed by a number, which indicates the order in which the comments
are responded to in Chapter 5 of this Final EIR.

text.document:
Available Business Resources – March 17, 2020
Dear Business Owner,
If you operate a business, nonprofit or are self-employed and have been impacted by COVID-19, please
take the City’s COVID-19 Business Impact Survey at www.oaklandbusinesscenter.com. This will serve as
the intake method for businesses seeking assistance. The online survey is available in English, Chinese,
Spanish and Vietnamese.
The City wants to share a variety of resources to support small businesses and workers during the
COVID-19 pandemic.
The City has launched a web page at www.oaklandbusinesscenter.com to serve as a portal for all the
local, state and federal resources available to support small businesses and workers during this crisis.
New federal and state programs on emergency funding and commercial eviction protections are
advancing through the legislative process. Concurrently, with help from private philanthropic partners,
the City is actively exploring funding opportunities to help vulnerable small businesses, nonprofits, and
the self-employed who have experienced losses related to COVID-19. The data that you and other
business owners have submitted through the survey will help inform the proposed local program. Once
the details on these new programs and resources have been confirmed, we will add that information to
the web page listed above.
Currently, the following resources and information are all available now on
www.oaklandbusinesscenter.com:
Help with Capital for Small Businesses
There are a number of resources available now, or in formation, that can provide capital to help sustain
your business during this crisis.
KIVA.org, a City of Oakland partner, offers zero-interest loans via crowdsourcing to entrepreneurs and
small business owners. In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, KIVA has raised its maximum loan
amount to $15,000, expanded eligibility for loans, and has extended the repayment grace period up to
six months post-loan disbursal for greater financial flexibility.
There are other local business providers who offer loans and technical assistance specifically to Oakland
small businesses, including, among others:
Main Street Launch: www.mainstreetlaunch.org/oakland-launch
Working Solutions: http://www.workingsolutions.org/news/2020/3/16/working-solutions-covid-19-
response
Pacific Community Ventures: www.pacificcommunityventures.org
In addition, the SBA’s low-interest Economic Injury Disaster Loans provides small businesses with
working capital loans of up to $2 million that may be used to pay fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable
and other bills that can’t be paid due to the disaster. Businesses with credit available elsewhere are not
eligible. https://disasterloan.sba.gov/ela/
Finally, the State of California’s Small Business Finance Center provides loan guarantees and direct loans
for small businesses that experience capital access barriers through its Disaster Relief Loan Guarantee
Program. https://www.ibank.ca.gov/small-business-finance-center/
Resources to Support Workforce Reductions
If you’re reducing your workforce, please consider the state’s Work Sharing Program that helps
employers minimize or eliminate the need for layoffs, keep trained employees and quickly prepare
when business conditions improve. The program helps employees whose hours and wages have been
reduced to receive Unemployment Insurance (UI) benefits.
https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/Work_Sharing_Program.htm
Information About State Unemployment & Disability Insurance Benefits –Waiting Periods Waived
Governor Newsom’s Executive Order on March 12, 2020, waives the one-week waiting period for people
who are unemployed and/or disabled as a result of COVID-19 to seek unemployment and disability
benefits. Please direct affected workers to the State website at
https://edd.ca.gov/about_edd/coronavirus-2019.htm to review what benefits are available including
sick leave, paid family leave and workers’ compensation benefits. The site also includes resources for
businesses, including tax deferrals.
Self-employed workers, including independent contractors, may be eligible for benefits if they have
elected to pay into Disability Insurance Elective Coverage (DIEC) under State Disability Insurance. For
more information, see the Elective Coverage for Employers and Self-Employed Individuals (DE 231EC) at
https://edd.ca.gov/pdf_pub_ctr/de231ec.pdf
City of Oakland’s Paid Sick Leave Requirement for Workers
The City is reminding all employers and workers of Oakland’s voter-approved sick leave benefits. During
the COVID-19 pandemic, it is important that workers have the ability to take paid time off when they are
sick. Measure FF, www.oaklandca.gov/topics/measure-ff-and-measure-z, voter-approved in November
2014, requires the accrual of paid sick leave for any individuals employed in Oakland. The minimum rate
of accrual is one hour paid sick leave for every 30 hours worked. Employers with less than 10 employees
must allow employees to accrue up to 40 hours of paid sick leave at a time and larger employers with 10
or more employees must allow employees to accrue at least 72 hours of paid sick leave. If you as an
employer have any questions, please reach out to minwageinfo@oaklandca.gov.
Help with Mounting Housing Costs and Residential Displacement
Through the Keep Oakland Housed program (https://www.keepoaklandhoused.org/), services are
available to all Oakland residents who are at risk of losing their housing. In addition to emergency
financial assistance to help with rent, utility payments, and other housing-related costs, the program
offers supportive services and legal representation for tenants with an active eviction lawsuit. If you or
any of your employees are at-risk for residential displacement, please connect with Keep Oakland
Housed.
Oakland City Council has taken first steps to halt residential evictions, with a proposed ordinance that
would halt evictions caused by income disruptions resulting from the COVID-19 pandemic.
www.oaklandca.gov
Direct Technical Help for Small Businesses
Finally, the City’s business development staff will contact Business Impact Survey respondents that
requested one-on-one follow-up shortly. They can connect you with Oakland’s many business support
organizations that offer financial products, technical assistance and other services to help local small
businesses during this pandemic.
Thank you for your investment in Oakland. Businesses like yours are essential to the vitality of the city
we call home.
